name: Amber Ratchet
description: Amber Ratchet is a small, dense world whose exposed metallic core gleams like polished bronze through a massive equatorial crater. The thin atmosphere scatters light into perpetual amber tones, giving the rocky terrain a warm glow that belies its frigid temperatures. Jagged ridges of iron-rich stone radiate outward from the crater in stepped formations, each shelf clicking downward like the teeth of some planetary ratchet mechanism.

The silence on Amber Ratchet is near-absolute, broken only by the faint whistle of thin winds threading through narrow canyons. The cold bites quickly through any exposed skin, yet the ground itself radiates a subtle warmth from the planet's still-active core. Magnetic anomalies play tricks on instruments and senses alike, creating phantom lights that dance along the ridge lines at irregular intervals.

A mining consortium operated here for three decades before abandoning their complex under mysterious circumstances, leaving behind functional equipment and half-filled cargo containers. Their final logs reference unusual magnetic interference that scrambled navigation systems and something they called the ratchet pulse, a rhythmic electromagnetic burst from the exposed core that grew stronger over time. The microbial colonies that thrive in the warm rock around the core seem to respond to these pulses, expanding and contracting in synchrony.

The platinum and uranium deposits remain largely untapped, drawing interest from salvage crews willing to brave the magnetic disruptions. The abandoned mining complex offers shelter but has been reported as difficult to leave, with navigation equipment failing in unpredictable ways. Some prospectors swear the ratchet pulse has a pattern that, once heard, becomes impossible to ignore, pulling the mind toward the glowing core like a mechanism winding itself tighter.
